record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: Are the asymptotic brane solutions obtained in the Robertson-Walker braneworld problems stable under general inhomogeneous perturbations, and what does function counting imply about the degree of generality of the regular and singular asymptotic behaviors that are found?

evidence.quote:
4.4 Genericity of the asymptotic solutions
In this project the aim is to examine, through a generic perturbation analysis, whether the found solutions are stable when we consider general inhomogeneous perturbations. Through function counting, we may be able to conclude about the degree of generality of the found brane asymptotics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Robertson–Walker braneworld model, namely a 4-dimensional brane carrying a spatially homogeneous and isotropic Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric, embedded in a 5-dimensional bulk spacetime, with the brane dynamics governed by the modified Einstein/Friedmann equations that arise from the Israel junction conditions (including the quadratic-in-energy-momentum correction and the Weyl "dark radiation" projection). For such a model with matter content given by a perfect fluid (or scalar field) of generic equation of state, suppose one has classified the formal asymptotic solutions of the brane evolution equations near the cosmological boundaries (past/future, in either finite or infinite proper time), obtaining a list of regular asymptotic behaviors and singular asymptotic behaviors.

(a) Determine whether each such asymptotic brane solution is stable when the homogeneity assumption is dropped, i.e. under general inhomogeneous (and anisotropic) linear perturbations of the brane metric and matter fields compatible with the bulk Einstein equations and the junction conditions.

(b) Using the method of function counting (counting the number of physically independent arbitrary functions of the spatial coordinates that parametrize the family of perturbed solutions, and comparing with the maximal number allowed by the order of the system modulo gauge and constraint equations), decide the degree of generality of each regular and each singular asymptotic regime: which behaviors are generic (carry the full complement of arbitrary functions), which are non-generic (carry strictly fewer arbitrary functions), and quantify the codimension of each non-generic family.
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on Robertson–Walker braneworld perturbations exists (e.g., large-scale perturbations and isotropy of the singularity, dynamical systems analyses of braneworld stability), but a comprehensive genericity/function-counting classification of all regular and singular asymptotic brane solutions under general inhomogeneous perturbations does not appear to have been completed; the problem is framed as a research project and no decisive resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Large-scale perturbations on the brane and the isotropy of the cosmological singularity
status_evidence.snippet: Studies large-scale inhomogeneous perturbations on the brane and the isotropy of the cosmological singularity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on inhomogeneous perturbations of brane cosmologies exist but do not exhaust the asymptotic classification.

status_evidence.title: Braneworld cosmological solutions and their stability
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates stability of braneworld cosmological solutions via dynamical systems methods.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of braneworld solutions has been investigated mainly via dynamical systems within homogeneous classes.
